key_insight: OMOP covered most demographics and medical history data in ENIGMA-SR, but had much weaker coverage for complex stroke rehabilitation assessments, especially subscales and items.
clinical_relevance: Standardizing rehabilitation research data with OMOP could make multi-site stroke datasets more interoperable for AI/ML and precision rehabilitation studies.
method: Two raters mapped 46 demographics/medical history variables and 95 rehabilitation assessments to OMOP concepts.
They evaluated agreement on OMOP inclusion and specific concept selection, then reconciled differences.
Coverage was analyzed for overall inclusion and for finer-grained subscale/item-level assessment data.
evidence_signal: Initial agreement was good to very good (Gwets AC 0.79-0.89), with OMOP inclusion of 84.8% for demographics/medical history versus 58.9% for rehabilitation assessments, and only 9.4% and 19.2% coverage for subscale- and item-level data.
watch_item: OMOP mapping may not capture the detail of many rehabilitation instruments, so some meaningful research variables could be lost or require custom extensions.
paper_title: Exploring the Application of the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model to Multi-site Stroke Rehabilitation Research Data
